stemMd: Suppose Study 1 had included trays of Variety S held at a soil water content of 25%. Based on Table 1, the germination percentage of those trays would most likely have been closest to:
explanationMd:
An interpolation question asks you to slot a new value **between two rows you already have**. A soil water content of 25% lies between the 20% row and the 30% row, so read only those two rows of the Variety S germination column:

- At 20% water: $78\%$ germination
- At 30% water: $74\%$ germination

Because 25% is halfway between the two water contents, the expected germination is roughly halfway between the two percentages:

$$\frac{78 + 74}{2} = \frac{152}{2} = 76$$

Check the answer by asking whether it is bracketed correctly: a value at 25% water must lie between 74% and 78%, and only $76\%$ does. Any choice outside that interval can be rejected without any arithmetic at all — that bracketing test is the fastest way to handle interpolation items.

distractorRationale.c: This is the Variety S value at 10% soil water content. It comes from reading the wrong row entirely; 25% water lies between the 20% and 30% rows, nowhere near 10%.
distractorRationale.b: This is the Variety R value at 40% water. It uses the wrong variety's column and the wrong row, and it falls outside the 74%-to-78% interval that any value at 25% water must lie in.
distractorRationale.d: This extrapolates an increasing trend that the data do not show. Variety S germination has already begun to fall by 30% water, so a value at 25% cannot exceed the 78% measured at 20% water, let alone reach 90%.

accessibilityText: The question asks for the likely germination percentage of Variety S at 25 percent soil water content, a value not tested. In Table 1, Variety S germinated 78 percent at 20 percent water and 74 percent at 30 percent water. The four choices are 42 percent, 62 percent, 76 percent and 90 percent.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Variety S germination is 78% at 20% water and 74% at 30%, so 25% interpolates to about (78 + 74)/2 = 76%. (d) 90% exceeds both bracketing values and (b) 62% / (c) 42% fall well outside the interval.

review.notes: Author solved the item and attempted to defend each distractor before keying it. A value at 25% water must be bracketed by the 20% and 30% readings, 78% and 74%, so 76% is the only option inside the admissible interval. Awaiting an independent blind solve. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
